text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing agitation, yellowing of your skin and eyes, and have abnormal lab results. To understand the cause, have you noticed any recent changes in your urine color, such as it appearing dark like tea?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CBC results show normal white blood cell counts and platelets, which makes acute bacterial infection or disseminated intravascular coagulation less likely. Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior, cocaine use, and the presence of jaundice and agitation, have you experienced any flu-like symptoms, muscle pain, or dark urine in the last two weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis C with Cocaine-induced Hepatotoxicity. The clinical picture of jaundice, agitation, high-risk sexual behavior, and recreational drug use is most consistent with an acute viral hepatitis superimposed on toxin-induced liver injury, rather than acute appendicitis.
